correctness.rationale: For any compared root edges either one endpoint overlaps (intersection comparison reduces to membership of b,c) or they are disjoint (membership on two disjoint pairs must balance). These exactly give A and D. Their counts and size crossing at n=5 produce the threshold. Connected-component union of a size-two cut identifies D subset A only at n=6 (besides n=4 A inside D); equal-size n=5 shapes are distinct. The Kneser diameter-two complement relation preserves equality of distances, including separate treatment of compared vertices. Independent BFS enumeration and maximality checks through n=10, plus full small-graph subset checks, all succeed. Finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: Infinite-family worst-case resolving-set robustness grows quadratically despite ordinary metric dimension growing linearly. Exact inclusion-maximal failure sets have a second structurally distinct, smaller family at all n>=7, and three exception transitions n=4,5,6. These are motivated structural and counting refinements for canonical graph families, not a mere substitution or single arbitrary small case.
